summary: npm package ships obfuscated PowerShell.NET-assembly loader disguised as document files
details: serpacksven@1.0.4 contains no JavaScript source and no legitimate library surface. package.json declares main=index.js, but the referenced file is absent from the tarball and no install/preinstall/postinstall/prepare lifecycle hooks are defined. The entire shipped payload is a single PowerShell script duplicated as seven identical files under document-like extensions (client, client.doc, client-for-you.doc, client.for.you.doc, json.txt, and variants) to defeat extension-based filtering and mislead inspection. The script hides the console window, then base64-decodes and XOR-decodes (key 89) a large embedded blob and reflectively loads it as a.NET assembly via a dynamically-constructed [System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load invocation, calling the EntryPoint of the in-memory assembly. The loader is padded with hundreds of junk variables and string-replace noise to frustrate static inspection. The package has no non-malicious purpose; it is a staging vehicle for an in-memory.NET payload that executes if any of the disguised files is run on a Windows host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
